mcq.q: If \( f(x) \) satisfies \( f(2\pi - x) = f(x) \) on \( (0, 2\pi) \), what can be said about its Fourier series?

sq.q: \(\text{Explain why constant term is } \frac{a_0}{2} \text{ instead of } a_0.\)
answer: \(\text{Constant term written as } \frac{a_0}{2} \text{ for consistency with } a_n \text{ formula when } n=0\)
\(a_0 = \frac{1}{\pi} \int_c^{c+2\pi} f(x) dx \text{ (same formula as } a_n \text{ with } n=0)\)
\(\text{Then } \frac{a_0}{2} = \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_c^{c+2\pi} f(x) dx, \text{ which is average value of } f(x)\)

sq.q: \(\text{Compare Fourier series formulas for intervals } (0,2\pi), (-\pi,\pi), \text{ and } (0,2l).\)
answer: \(\text{All have form: } f(x) = \frac{a_0}{2} + \sum (a_n \cos \omega_n x + b_n \sin \omega_n x)\)

Step Marks Compute \(a_0=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)dx=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi}x\,dx=\frac{\pi}{2}\) (2) \(a_n=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)\cos nx\,dx=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi}x\cos nx\,dx=\frac{(-1)^n-1}{\pi n^2}\) (3) \(b_n=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)\sin nx\,dx=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi}x\sin nx\,dx=\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n}\) (3) Thus, \(f(x)=\frac{\pi}{4}+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left[\frac{(-1)^n-1}{\pi n^2}\cos nx+\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n}\sin nx\right]\) (2) Put \(x=0\): \(0=\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{2}{\pi}\left[\frac{1}{1^2}+\frac{1}{3^2}+\frac{1}{5^2}+...\right]\) ⇒ \(\frac{1}{1^2}+\frac{1}{3^2}+\frac{1}{5^2}+...=\frac{\pi^2}{8}\) (5)
